library_preparation_preflight.summary: No extra dependency/Docker/env setup needed. The two tests that boot a real AnnotationConfigApplicationContext through @EnableSpringConfigured / @Enable*(mode = AdviceMode.ASPECTJ) trigger CGLIB runtime-enhancement of spring-aspects' own full-mode @Configuration classes (SpringConfiguredConfiguration, AspectJTransactionManagementConfiguration, AspectJAsyncConfiguration, AspectJCachingConfiguration) and ASM-based classpath-resource reads of selector classes (e.g. AsyncConfigurationSelector.class) — both unsupported/unregistered under Native Image. Rewrite those tests to exercise the aspects directly instead.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Do not exercise @EnableSpringConfigured, @EnableTransactionManagement(mode = AdviceMode.ASPECTJ), @EnableCaching(mode = AdviceMode.ASPECTJ), or @EnableAsync(mode = AdviceMode.ASPECTJ) through a real AnnotationConfigApplicationContext.refresh() in the generated 6.0.0 test. Spring's ConfigurationClassPostProcessor CGLIB-enhances the library's own internal full @Configuration classes (org.springframework.context.annotation.aspectj.SpringConfiguredConfiguration, org.springframework.transaction.aspectj.AspectJTransactionManagementConfiguration, org.springframework.scheduling.aspectj.AspectJAsyncConfiguration, org.springframework.cache.aspectj.AspectJCachingConfiguration/AspectJJCacheConfiguration) at runtime, and also triggers ASM-based classpath-resource reads of selector classes such as org/springframework/scheduling/annotation/AsyncConfigurationSelector.class and org/springframework/context/annotation/aspectj/SpringConfiguredConfiguration.class, which fail as missing resources under Native Image. There is no reachability-metadata fix for the runtime CGLIB class definition. Instead cover these aspects the way the passing majority of the existing 5.3.31 suite already does: obtain the aspect via its static aspectOf() accessor (AnnotationBeanConfigurerAspect.aspectOf(), AnnotationTransactionAspect.aspectOf(), AnnotationCacheAspect.aspectOf(), AnnotationAsyncExecutionAspect.aspectOf()) and configure/invoke it directly, or use GenericInterfaceDrivenDependencyInjectionAspect directly, instead of booting a full ApplicationContext through the @Enable* annotations.
risks: Dropping the ApplicationContext-driven @Enable*(mode=ASPECTJ)/@EnableSpringConfigured flow means the 6.0.0 test loses coverage of Spring's bean-registration/@Configuration integration path that the 5.3.31 suite does exercise — this is an inherent Native Image limitation (runtime CGLIB class definition on the library's own full-mode @Configuration classes), not a scaffold or dependency gap, so it cannot be recovered via metadata.

This is likely a generic risk for other spring-* modules moving to the stricter current-defaults native-image mode wherever a library ships its own full-mode @Configuration classes, not unique to spring-aspects 6.0.0.
